deep.reconstruction:
This page proves the theorem stated on the previous page about Hilbert–Schmidt operators between Hilbert spaces. The exposition treats L^2(E,F) as the Hilbert tensor product \bar E \otimes^{(2)} F.

(1) Ideal property. Let (e_i) be an orthonormal basis of E and A: F→G bounded. Then
 Σ‖A u e_i‖² ≤ Σ‖A‖²‖u e_i‖² = ‖A‖² Σ‖u e_i‖².
So Au is Hilbert–Schmidt and ‖Au‖_2 ≤ ‖A‖‖u‖_2. A crossed-out attempt follows. The right-multiplication case uA is presumably deduced from the left case via adjoints, i.e. from (2).

(2) Adjoint. The conjugate Hilbert space \overline{\bar E \otimes^{(2)} F} identifies, by 'formule 8' (conjugate of a Hilbert tensor product), with \bar{\bar E} \otimes^{(2)} \bar F = E \otimes^{(2)} \bar F. By the symmetry of the Hilbert tensor product this is isomorphic to \bar F \otimes^{(2)} E. Hence there is a Hilbert-space isomorphism \overline{L^2(E,F)} ≅ L^2(F,E). One checks directly that it is u ↦ u*. This gives u HS ⇔ u* HS, with ‖u‖_2 = ‖u*‖_2 and (u,v) = (v*,u*).

(3) Modulus. Take the polar decomposition u = Uh, where h = √(u*u) and U: E→F is a partial isometry. Also h = Vu with V = U* a partial isometry F→E. Applying (1) in both directions, with ‖U‖,‖V‖ ≤ 1, gives ‖u‖_2 ≤ ‖h‖_2 ≤ ‖u‖_2, so ‖u‖_2 = ‖h‖_2. The next page diagonalises h in an orthonormal basis to get ‖h‖_2 = (Σρ_i²)^{1/2}. It then passes to the analogous statements for 'opérateurs de Fredholm' (nuclear/trace-class operators, ‖u‖_1 = ‖h‖_1 = Σρ_i).

Purpose: this is an expository section of Grothendieck's 1953 functional-analysis notes. It recalls the Hilbert–Schmidt and trace-class theory in the tensor-product language used in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires'.
errors: No mathematical errors. The proof of the right-ideal case uA is not written out; it is presumably deduced via (2): (uA)* = A*u*.

The proof of (2) relies on 'formule 8' (identifying the conjugate of a Hilbert tensor product) and on the symmetry \bar F⊗E ≅ E⊗\bar F. Both are standard; the verification that the isomorphism is u ↦ u* is asserted ('on vérifie aussitôt') without detail.

ideas.what: Hilbert–Schmidt operators form a two-sided ideal with ‖AuB‖_2 ≤ ‖A‖‖u‖_2‖B‖
ideas.modern_name: Ideal property of the Schatten class S_2
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Mem. AMS 16, 1955)

ideas.what: Identification L^2(E,F) ≅ \bar E ⊗^{(2)} F, and \overline{L^2(E,F)} ≅ L^2(F,E) via u ↦ u*
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert–Schmidt operators as Hilbert tensor product; adjoint as antiunitary flip
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955), chapter on Hilbert spaces

ideas.what: ‖u‖_2 = ‖√(u*u)‖_2 via polar decomposition and partial isometries
ideas.modern_name: Polar decomposition; Schatten norms depend only on singular values

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook proofs of the basic properties of Hilbert–Schmidt operators (ideal property, adjoint, modulus via polar decomposition), written in tensor-product language. All of this is classical and appears in Grothendieck's own published memoir; nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The tensor symbols are not \hat\otimes / \check\otimes but ⊗ with a superscript '(2)' (Hilbert tensor product): read 'Ē ⊗^{(2)} F'.

Line 'que de Ē⊗F sur Ē⊗F' is better read as '... conjugué de Ē⊗^{(2)}F, \overline{Ē⊗^{(2)}F}, qui peut s'identifier à \bar{\bar E}⊗^{(2)}\bar F (formule 8) = E⊗^{(2)}\bar F, donc ... isomorphe à \bar F⊗^{(2)}E'. The bars over F are present in the image.
The isomorphism is of \overline{L^2(E,F)} (overlined) onto L^2(F,E); the overline over L^2(E,F) is visible in the image.
In part 3, 'h = Vu' — 'h' is written over an initial 'R' or similar.
